$BTC Has sold off -28% in the weeks before both the $SPCX and $ANT IPO's.

Plenty of arguments as to why it happened, but one of them is the need for liquidity to put into these IPO's.

The Anthropic sale is expected to raise ~$90B. SpaceX did ~$85B.

That liquidity has to come from somewhere, including high risk liquid assets like Bitcoin and Crypto. Even if it's just a fraction, it still counts. Also considering the frontrunning of this.

tweets.text:
I'm not interested in trading bounces during a medium-term downtrend.

I'm not saying it's right or wrong. It's simply not my business.

I know my strengths and weaknesses extremely well. I know how to ride trends until they become exhausted, and I've been demonstrating that since 2017/18.

My business is buying and selling at extremes.

That doesn't mean I always catch the exact top or bottom. But when I finally pull the trigger, there's usually very little room left for the trend to continue.

Most people think being successful in this market means trading every single move.

I completely disagree.

In my experience, there are maybe 1 or 2 truly worthwhile opportunities per year.

The rest is mostly noise.

And here's what most people don't understand:

The time between one extreme and the next is exactly where people lose their minds.

They get impatient. They chase moves. They overtrade. They convince themselves they're missing opportunities.

Meanwhile, I'm perfectly comfortable doing absolutely nothing.

Patience is part of my strategy, not a lack of one.

If you understand this approach and want to follow my analysis more closely, join the @AlphaDoctrine_x  waitlist.

It closes in 12 days.

https://alphadoctrine.io

We keep going.

Trying to trade $ANT in an attempt to catch the initial rally is completely illogical.

The crash will be heavy.
